finding: the LIVE solar_iag NIR Fe I 1D-LTE Codex product predates RYA-1191's `pipeline.fit_validity` guard and its aggregate contains FOUR non-convergent fits.
how_it_surfaced: NIR holds no lab Fe line above the depth gate, so the Reference pool and the Codex pool are the SAME LINES. The Reference run therefore re-measured this cell on today's code, and the two products disagree on n: 28 rows with 26 in-aggregate in the committed Codex per-line file against 22 in the guarded run. That is a POOL difference, not drift, and it was visible only because the two pools are provably identical.
scale: each is 1.75-2.58 dex from solar, across a bound that spans a factor of ~1000 in abundance -- RYA-1191's own framing: 'a NON-CONVERGENT FIT, not an outlier'. 9437.793 is the very line RYA-1191 named as the bad fit behind the refuted 1.315 dex Kitt Peak dispersion; it is still in the aggregate here.
effect_on_the_published_value: SMALL on the median and LARGE on the dispersion. The published A moves 7.546 -> 7.554 (+0.008) because the product aggregates by median and four wild points scatter both ways; the line-to-line scatter the bar is built from does not survive them.
why_it_was_missed: RYA-1203 re-ingested the two STALE KP NIR Fe I entries onto the guarded pool (1D-LTE n=26 -> 23, ENGINE-A n=7 -> 6) and did not reach the IAG one. Two of three.
status: MEASURED, and the corrected artifact exists. Whether it replaces the live row is a value decision on a Codex product, which this ticket does not own -- flagged to Ryan in the EOS rather than settled here.

paired_re_run.method: the GRADED selector re-run on this commit, same holding, same window
paired_re_run.verdict: CONFIRMED. Today's code on the SAME selector drops the four non-convergent fits and returns 7.554 at n=22. The live row is a pre-guard artifact; nothing about the measurement is in dispute.
